meta.scope: Indonesia Batch 10 — Strategic maritime chokepoints (Malacca, Sunda, Lombok, Makassar), inter-provincial / inter-island trade, special economic & free-trade zones, and the policy/regulatory reflection of archipelagic diversity. Defines Indonesia’s position on critical energy and trade routes with exceptional care.
meta.strategy_note: User emphasis: many islands → diversity in policy/regulation/trade; inter-provincial commerce; Indonesia sits on vital trade routes through which much of Asia’s energy from the Middle East passes.

candidates.title: Strait of Malacca — strategic chokepoint and transit statistics/context
candidates.publisher: Derived from international maritime/energy analyses + Indonesian sovereignty context (Sumatra side)
candidates.description: The primary western gateway between the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea / Pacific. Handles a very large share of global maritime trade and an even larger share of seaborne energy flows from the Middle East and Africa to East Asia. Indonesia controls a significant portion of the southern coastline. Continuously cited in energy-security, shipping and geopolitical analysis.
candidates.notes: Highest-centrality maritime-chokepoint node for Indonesia. Critical for understanding why the archipelago sits at the centre of Asian energy security.

candidates.title: Sunda Strait — alternative passage statistics/context
candidates.publisher: Derived from maritime and Indonesian official context
candidates.description: Major alternative route between the Indian Ocean and the Java Sea / internal Indonesian waters. Shallower and more constrained than Lombok; used as a partial substitute when Malacca is stressed. Fully under Indonesian sovereignty.
candidates.notes: Key alternative-passage node under full Indonesian control.

candidates.title: Lombok and Makassar Straits — deep-water alternative passages
candidates.publisher: Derived from maritime analyses + Indonesian sovereignty
candidates.description: Deep-water alternative routes preferred by the largest deep-draft tankers and bulk carriers (especially when Malacca draft is limiting) and by traffic linked to Australia. Also strategically relevant for submarine transit. Entirely within Indonesian archipelagic waters.
referenced_by: Australian and East Asian trade-route studies
candidates.notes: Deep-water redundancy nodes that raise Indonesia’s strategic maritime centrality.

candidates.title: Indonesian Archipelagic Sea Lanes (ALKI) and archipelagic-state regime
candidates.description: The formal Archipelagic Sea Lanes (ALKI) designated under the archipelagic-state regime of UNCLOS. Legal and operational frame that governs transit through Indonesian waters while preserving sovereignty. Recurring citation in maritime policy, defence and international-law contexts.
referenced_by: Malacca, Sunda, Lombok and Makassar nodes
candidates.notes: Foundational legal-regime node for all Indonesian chokepoint and transit analysis.

candidates.title: Inter-provincial / inter-regional trade statistics (Perdagangan Antar Wilayah)
candidates.description: Official BPS publication on inter-provincial trade — purchases and sales of goods between provinces, trade maps, and modes of transport. Captures the domestic commercial circulation that links Java, Sumatra, Kalimantan, Sulawesi, Papua and the other islands.
candidates.notes: Core domestic-commerce node. Shows that Indonesia is not only an international transit state but also a complex internal trading system across thousands of islands.

candidates.title: Inter-island trade volume and value (selected commodity series)
candidates.description: Statistics on inter-island movements of food crops and other commodities. Complements the broader inter-provincial trade publication with commodity-specific domestic flow data.
candidates.notes: Commodity-flow densification of the domestic-trade cluster.

candidates.title: Special Economic Zones (KEK) statistics and regulatory framework
candidates.publisher: Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs / KEK administration / related
candidates.description: Regulatory framework and performance statistics for Indonesia’s Special Economic Zones (Kawasan Ekonomi Khusus). Includes tax holidays, customs facilities, VAT treatment and investment incentives designed to attract industry to designated locations across the archipelago.
candidates.notes: Policy instrument that explicitly tries to shape industrial location across a diverse archipelago.

candidates.title: Free Trade and Free Port Zones (KPBPB / FTZ) — Batam, Bintan, Karimun, Sabang
candidates.publisher: Directorate General of Customs / related legal framework
candidates.description: Free Trade and Free Port Zones with separate customs treatment (duty, VAT, excise relief). Batam–Bintan–Karimun form the principal FTZ complex facing Singapore and the Malacca approaches; Sabang is the western outlier. Legal basis in successive laws and implementing regulations.
referenced_by: Malacca Strait and Riau Islands regional analysis
candidates.notes: Customs-and-tariff regime node that sits directly on the approaches to the Malacca Strait.

candidates.title: Customs, tariff and trade-facilitation regime
candidates.publisher: Directorate General of Customs and Excise / Ministry of Finance / Ministry of Trade
candidates.description: The broader customs and tariff framework that governs both international and (indirectly) domestic trade. Includes preferential treatment under ASEAN, RCEP and bilateral arrangements, as well as the special regimes applied inside SEZs and FTZs.
candidates.notes: Umbrella regulatory node for tariff and border treatment.

candidates.title: Inter-island connectivity and logistics policy/statistics
candidates.publisher: Derived from BPS transport statistics, Ministry of Transportation, and connectivity programmes
candidates.description: Statistical and policy traces of inter-island shipping, port connectivity and logistics programmes intended to reduce price disparities and integrate the domestic market across the archipelago.
candidates.notes: Domestic-integration counterpart to the international chokepoint nodes.

candidates.title: Indonesia maritime-chokepoint, inter-provincial trade and special-zone meta-node
candidates.publisher: Derived from maritime, BPS trade, SEZ/FTZ and customs sources
candidates.description: Meta-node that binds the Strait of Malacca, Sunda Strait, Lombok–Makassar passages, Archipelagic Sea Lanes regime, inter-provincial and inter-island trade statistics, Special Economic Zones, Free Trade/Free Port Zones, customs/tariff regime, and inter-island connectivity policy into a single high-centrality cluster. Captures both Indonesia’s role as a global energy and trade transit state and its internal commercial diversity across thousands of islands.
referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Energy, trade, provincial and external-sector series from earlier batches
candidates.notes: High-mass integrating node for the strategic-geography and internal-diversity layer requested by the user.
